clock_test.authority: JPL Horizons Earth center and Sun center state vectors versus solar-system barycenter, ICRF with TIME_TYPE=TDB and VEC_CORR=NONE. Independent conventional comparison uses Astropy bundled ephemeris without downloads. Time pairs use UTC versus TDB, geometric uncorrected versus heliocentric or barycentric, and conservative ground-to-geocenter plus TESS topocenter allowance.
clock_test.decision: Define indistinguishable as less than the larger of 120 s and three combined timing scales, adding the 2 s site/instrument allowance. Test both frozen inner fits and the c fit. If every plausible conversion and half-day bookkeeping variant remains outside the threshold, reject only the registered common-clock aliases. Do not assign the underlying error or establish a physical transit.
clock_test.methods: For the same literal disputed number, convert JD_UTC, JD_TDB, BJD_UTC, BJD_TDB, HJD_UTC and HJD_TDB to BJD_TDB. Iterate inverse light-time to tolerance below 0.001 s. Compare each JPL and Astropy conversion within 0.1 s at geocenter. Allow a deliberately generous independent site/instrument margin of 2 s. Treat noon/midnight bookkeeping separately as signed half-day shifts.
clock_test.negative_control: Shift the known center to a synthetic conventional clock representation and require recovery at sub-0.1 s. A response with incorrect frame, center, ephemeris interval or units must fail admission.

forecast_and_operation: No new calendar forecast or observing action. This confirmation concerns timing-scope admission only.
input_selection: Use UTC calendar April 2023 for coverage and 2023-04-21 to 2023-04-29 for JPL vectors. Use only the disputed raw numeric timing and the already frozen Sector 64 inner and outer fitted references for classification. Positive ASAS-SN archive control comes from the same target and month, requiring any public April time rows before interpreting sparse coverage as a source-specific negative. If public data is unavailable, acquisition is BLOCKED rather than zero. No other epoch counts as a physical confirmation.

physical_admission.calendar_and_bjd_windows: Signed midpoint frequency and time bounds are recorded for the catalogue center, frozen c reference and nearest b reference. Each contact interval uses the corresponding prior frozen b or c duration, with an exterior hour on each side.
physical_admission.endpoint: ASAS-SN public Sky Patrol v2 target match anchored by TIC, or the official legacy public coordinate form if no anonymous documented v2 path works
physical_admission.minimum_gate: Require independent photons, verified target, calibrated flux and uncertainty, documented timestamps and observatory or time correction, and at least three quality-good observations each before first contact, across ingress, across egress, and after last contact. Each ingress and egress covers a quarter of the nominal duration as a generous first screen. Without coverage, do not fit or assert physical presence or absence. With coverage, preregister fit and attribution tests separately before opening flux values.

question: Can otherwise plausible clock standards explain the discrepant catalogue timing? Do independently collected public ASAS-SN exposures cover the disputed April 2023 windows with usable time and flux support?
